learning_outcomes.text: Analyzes and solves systems of linear equations. Knows how to discuss their nature.
Handles and correctly uses fundamental matrix algebra operations.
Calculates eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a matrix. Applies them in the discussion regarding the diagonalization of said matrix.
Manages vector algebra and geometry in the plane and in three-dimensional space.
Manages elementary geometric objects in the plane and in three-dimensional space using necessary equations.
Manages complex numbers and their geometric representation.
Calculates derivatives of functions using the chain rule.
Calculates and studies extrema of functions.
Solves problems involving the formulation of integrals (lengths, areas, volumes, etc.).
Can distinguish and solve differential equations: separable variables, homogeneous, linear, and exact.
Can apply the Laplace transform to differential equation problems.

syllabus_topics: Matrix Algebra. Systems of Linear Equations
Vectors in the Plane and in Three-Dimensional Space
teaching_methods: Practical classes in small groups (in-person) including exercises developed in writing or using mathematical software (wxMaxima or similar)
Study and preparation for theoretical classes
Study and preparation for practical classes
Attendance at in-person and/or virtual tutorials in small groups

assessment_methods.method: Second Partial Exam (Complex Numbers, Differential Calculus in One Variable)
Third Partial Exam (Integral Calculus in One Variable, Differential Equations)

assessment_rules: The course can be evaluated through continuous assessment, consisting of three partial exams, or a single final exam. Students can retake failed partial exams during the single evaluation exam slot in the first call. Continuous assessment is only valid for the first call. Students must opt for single evaluation via the virtual classroom before December 12, 2026, 23:59. In the second call, only a single evaluation exam is available.
